cancer_indication: Hormone receptor–positive, HER2-negative breast cancer (in combination with endocrine therapy for adjuvant therapy in stage II–III early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence, and for advanced/metastatic disease with an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant).
moa: Ribociclib is a selective inhibitor of CDK4 and CDK6, kinases that bind D-type cyclins and drive G1→S cell-cycle progression. By inhibiting CDK4/6, ribociclib prevents phosphorylation of the retinoblastoma protein (RB1), keeping RB1 in its hypophosphorylated, E2F-bound state and blocking E2F-mediated transcription required for the G1/S transition. This results in G1 cell-cycle arrest and reduced proliferation, and clinically deeper suppression of proliferation markers (e.g., Ki-67) when combined with endocrine therapy in HR+/HER2− breast cancer.

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: Represents transcriptional programs driven by E2F that enable S-phase entry and DNA replication, regulated by RB1 phosphorylation status.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: E2F-driven proliferation programs are central to HR+/HER2− breast cancer growth; suppressing E2F output via the CDK4/6–RB1 checkpoint is a key determinant of disease control with ribociclib-based therapy.

Sensitive: [Mechanistically accurate] High E2F-target output implies an active CDK4/6→RB→E2F axis with RB dependency; CDK4/6 blockade should collapse E2F transcription and growth. (Nature)
DrugBank:DB11730; ChEMBL:CHEMBL3545110; FDA label (Kisqali) 209092; PMID:35263519; NCT01958021
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] E2F targets can stay high despite CDK4/6 inhibition if RB1 is lost/defective or bypass occurs via cyclin/CDK rewiring, predicting intrinsic resistance. (Reactome)
PMID:29236940; PMID:27020857; Reactome:R-HSA-9659787

Sensitive: [Mechanistically rare] Low E2F may reflect slower cycling, yet tumors can still be RB-dependent and benefit from preventing cell-cycle re-entry under endocrine pressure. (PubMed)
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] Low E2F can indicate quiescence or alternative (RB-independent) drivers, reducing effective CDK4/6 target reliance → limited benefit. (ScienceDirect)
PMID: (review) Pandey 2019 (IJC); CDK4/6i resistance reviews

Sensitive: [Mechanistically accurate] On-treatment E2F target suppression is the expected pharmacodynamic consequence of RB hypophosphorylation → cytostatic tumor control. (FDA Access Data)
FDA label 209092; EMA EPAR; PMID:35263519
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] E2F can drop yet clinical resistance still emerge if survival pathways (e.g., PI3K/mTOR) sustain viability or resistant clones expand. (PubMed)

Sensitive: [Mechanistically not possible] Rising E2F targets while “sensitive” contradicts the core CDK4/6i mechanism; if E2F rises on therapy it typically signals inadequate inhibition or escape. (FDA Access Data)
FDA label 209092
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] Persistent/increasing E2F output indicates bypass (e.g., cyclin E/CDK2, CDK6 amp) or RB loss, consistent with resistance. (PubMed)

HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.description: Encompasses genes controlling progression through G2 and mitosis, including mitotic regulators that rise in proliferating tumors.
HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.interpretation: G2/M activity reflects high proliferative throughput in breast cancer; downstream mitotic programs diminish when upstream G1/S entry is blocked, linking this pathway to tumor proliferation state.

Sensitive: [Mechanistically accurate] High G2/M checkpoint signature reflects a highly cycling state; if RB is intact, proliferative HR+ tumors can still be CDK4/6-dependent and respond. (ScienceDirect)
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] High proliferation can also reflect RB-pathway defects or CDK2-driven cycling, reducing CDK4/6 dependence and predicting resistance. (Reactome)
Reactome:R-HSA-9659787; PMID:36071033; PMID:30511015

Sensitive: [Mechanistically rare] Low mitotic program may still benefit if endocrine-driven cells intermittently cycle and remain RB-dependent; CDK4/6i can maintain arrest. (PubMed)
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] If baseline mitotic activity is very low, incremental benefit from a cytostatic cell-cycle drug may be limited (minimal target engagement). (ScienceDirect)
CDK4/6i resistance reviews

Sensitive: [Mechanistically accurate] CDK4/6 blockade enforces G1 arrest, reducing entry into S/G2/M and lowering G2/M checkpoint signatures in responders. (FDA Access Data)
FDA label 209092; EMA EPAR
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] Even with reduced cycling signatures, tumors may persist via survival/bypass programs (e.g., PI3K/mTOR activation) → resistant disease. (PubMed)

Sensitive: [Mechanistically not possible] Increased G2/M activity during effective CDK4/6 inhibition is inconsistent with true sensitivity; it usually indicates escape from arrest. (FDA Access Data)
FDA label 209092
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] Persistent mitotic signaling implies failure of G1 control and ongoing proliferation → resistance. (AACR Journals)

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: A growth and survival signaling axis that promotes proliferation and anti-apoptotic programs downstream of PI3K and AKT through mTOR.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling provides alternative growth and survival inputs in breast cancer and can reduce dependence on CDK4/6-mediated cell-cycle control, shaping therapeutic benefit and failure patterns.

Sensitive: [Mechanistically rare] PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation can coexist with RB dependence; some HR+ tumors still gain meaningful benefit from CDK4/6i + endocrine therapy. (PMC)
PMID:35263519; PMID: (review) Clark 2020
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] Activated PI3K/mTOR can promote survival and cell-cycle bypass, and is reported as a driver in CDK4/6i-resistant HR+ models. (PubMed)

Sensitive: [Mechanistically accurate] Lower PI3K/mTOR signaling reduces a major bypass/survival route, increasing reliance on the RB–E2F axis → better CDK4/6i sensitivity. (ScienceDirect)
Resistance: [Mechanistically rare] Resistance can still occur via RB loss, cyclin E/CDK2 activation, or other rewiring even without strong PI3K/mTOR activity. (PubMed)

Sensitive: [Mechanistically rare] Adaptive PI3K/mTOR feedback may rise on CDK4/6i, yet some tumors remain controlled if RB arrest is maintained and endocrine therapy suppresses upstream cues. (PubMed)
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] On-treatment PI3K/mTOR upshift is a documented resistance adaptation; PI3K/mTOR targeting can restore control in resistant HR+ models. (PubMed)

Sensitive: [Mechanistically accurate] With effective endocrine + CDK4/6 blockade and reduced tumor growth signaling, PI3K/mTOR signatures can decrease as part of response biology. (PubMed)
PMID:35263519; PMID: (Gul 2018 combo rationale)
Resistance: [Mechanistically rare] PI3K/mTOR can fall yet resistance persist via RB loss or cyclin E/CDK2-driven cycling. (PubMed)

HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP.description: Captures activation of MAPK/ERK-related signaling programs often driven by upstream receptor and growth-factor signaling inputs.
HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP.interpretation: MAPK/ERK-linked signaling can sustain proliferative signaling in breast cancer and contribute to reduced reliance on CDK4/6–RB1 gating, affecting durability of response to CDK4/6 inhibition.

Sensitive: [Mechanistically rare] MAPK/KRAS signatures may be elevated, but if downstream proliferation remains RB-dependent, CDK4/6 blockade can still impose arrest. (ScienceDirect)
MSigDB:M5953
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] KRAS/RTK/MAPK activation can sustain cyclin programs and contribute to CDK4/6i resistance; KRAS-mutated MBC has been described in the context of CDK4/6i resistance. (PubMed)

Sensitive: [Mechanistically accurate] Low KRAS/MAPK pressure reduces a common bypass route, increasing dependence on ER–cyclin D–CDK4/6–RB control. (PubMed)
Resistance: [Mechanistically rare] Resistance can still be mediated by RB1 defects or cyclin E/CDK2 rewiring independent of KRAS signaling. (Reactome)
Reactome:R-HSA-9659787; PMID:30511015

Sensitive: [Mechanistically rare] Some adaptive MAPK signaling can emerge without immediate clinical failure if RB-mediated arrest persists and endocrine suppression limits proliferative output. (PubMed)
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] Rising KRAS/MAPK programs on therapy commonly indicate escape signaling that sustains proliferation despite CDK4/6 inhibition → resistance. (PubMed)

Sensitive: [Mechanistically accurate] Reduced KRAS-signature may reflect broader growth signal suppression in responders (less upstream RTK drive as proliferation collapses). (PubMed)
PMID:35263519; FDA label 209092
Resistance: [Mechanistically rare] KRAS signaling may drop yet resistance persist through RB loss/cyclin E bypass. (PubMed)

REACTOME_CYCLIN_E_ASSOCIATED_EVENTS.description: Represents Cyclin E–linked events controlling late G1 to S-phase entry and related transcriptional and replication programs.
REACTOME_CYCLIN_E_ASSOCIATED_EVENTS.interpretation: Cyclin E/CDK2 activity can provide an alternative route to RB1 phosphorylation and S-phase entry in breast cancer, influencing how strongly tumors depend on cyclin D–CDK4/6 control.

Sensitive: [Mechanistically rare] Elevated cyclin E activity usually predicts escape, but in some tumors it may still be partially constrained by RB and remain targetable if CDK4/6 remains dominant. (ScienceDirect)
Reactome:R-HSA-69202; MSigDB:M14520
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] High cyclin E/CDK2 program provides a classic bypass around CDK4/6 inhibition and is repeatedly linked to acquired/intrinsic resistance. (PubMed)

Sensitive: [Mechanistically accurate] Low cyclin E/CDK2 bypass suggests greater dependence on cyclin D–CDK4/6–RB control → higher sensitivity. (ScienceDirect)
Resistance: [Mechanistically rare] Even with low cyclin E, RB1 defects can abolish CDK4/6i efficacy. (Reactome)
Reactome:R-HSA-9659787; PMID:29236940

Sensitive: [Mechanistically rare] Cyclin E upshift can occur transiently as an adaptation signal, but durable sensitivity would require RB arrest to remain dominant and adaptation not to fully bypass control. (PubMed)
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] On-therapy cyclin E/CDK2 escalation is a hallmark of escape from CDK4/6 arrest and is observed at resistance. (PubMed)
PMID:30511015; PMID: (Guarducci 2018) 30511015

Sensitive: [Mechanistically accurate] Effective G1 arrest reduces progression into cyclin E–CDK2-driven G1/S events; cyclin E program can fall with response. (FDA Access Data)
FDA label 209092; Reactome:R-HSA-69202
Resistance: [Mechanistically rare] Cyclin E may decrease yet resistance persist via RB loss or PI3K/mTOR survival rewiring. (PubMed)

WU_APOPTOSIS_BY_CDKN1A_VIA_TP53.description: Reflects TP53–CDKN1A (p21) checkpoint signaling that can reinforce cell-cycle arrest and is discussed in the context of CDK4/6 inhibitor response.
WU_APOPTOSIS_BY_CDKN1A_VIA_TP53.interpretation: TP53–p21 checkpoint integrity is relevant to breast cancer control under CDK4/6 inhibition because p21 levels correlate with ribociclib sensitivity and loss of this checkpoint is linked to reduced enforcement of arrest.

Sensitive: [Mechanistically rare] A primed p21/apoptosis transcriptional context could facilitate deeper responses beyond cytostasis in a subset of HR+ tumors. (gsea-msigdb.org)
MSigDB:WU_APOPTOSIS_BY_CDKN1A_VIA_TP53; PMID:35263519
Resistance: [Mechanistically rare] Even with an apoptosis-leaning signature, CDK4/6 inhibitors are often predominantly cytostatic; tumors can persist without undergoing apoptosis. (ScienceDirect)
CDK4/6i MOA references

Sensitive: [Mechanistically rare] Low baseline apoptosis doesn’t preclude growth arrest; ribociclib can still deliver benefit via RB-mediated cell-cycle suppression. (FDA Access Data)
FDA label 209092; PMID:35263519
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] A weak p21/p53-apoptosis context can support survival/tolerance to cytostatic stress, favoring persistence and eventual resistance. (PMC)
CDK4/6i resistance reviews; MSigDB set page

Sensitive: [Mechanistically rare] CDK4/6 inhibition can increase CDKN1A (p21) and senescence programs; apoptosis via this route can occur but is not the dominant clinical phenotype. (gsea-msigdb.org)
MSigDB:WU_APOPTOSIS_BY_CDKN1A_VIA_TP53
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] Upregulation of p21-related programs may reflect cell-cycle arrest without tumor eradication (tolerance/senescence-like persistence), enabling later resistance. (PMC)
CDK4/6i resistance reviews

Sensitive: [Mechanistically not possible] “Sensitivity” with suppression of an apoptosis-by-p21 program is internally inconsistent; if apoptosis programs fall, it would not explain improved killing. (gsea-msigdb.org)
MSigDB:WU_APOPTOSIS_BY_CDKN1A_VIA_TP53
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] Failure to engage p21/apoptosis biology alongside cytostasis supports persistence and resistance evolution. (PMC)

REACTOME_ABERRANT_REGULATION_OF_MITOTIC_.description: Represents dysregulated G1/S control caused by RB1 defects, disrupting the RB1–E2F checkpoint that normally constrains S-phase entry.
REACTOME_ABERRANT_REGULATION_OF_MITOTIC_.interpretation: RB1 defects undermine the central mechanistic node targeted by CDK4/6 inhibitors in breast cancer, limiting the ability of ribociclib to induce durable G1 arrest and thereby shaping intrinsic and acquired non-response.

Sensitive: [Mechanistically not possible] RB1-defect programs directly undermine CDK4/6i mechanism (requires functional RB); “RB1 defects + sensitivity” is contradictory. (Reactome)
Reactome:R-HSA-9659787; MSigDB:M38998
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] RB1 loss/defects are a core resistance mechanism because CDK4/6 inhibition works by maintaining RB-mediated E2F repression. (ScienceDirect)
Reactome:R-HSA-9659787; PMID:29236940

Sensitive: [Mechanistically accurate] Low RB1-defect signaling implies intact RB control, enabling the canonical CDK4/6i cytostatic mechanism. (ScienceDirect)
FDA label 209092; Reactome:R-HSA-9659787
Resistance: [Mechanistically rare] Even with apparently intact RB signatures, resistance can arise via cyclin E/CDK2 bypass or PI3K/mTOR rewiring. (PubMed)

Sensitive: [Mechanistically not possible] Therapy cannot induce RB1 defects and simultaneously improve response; enrichment of RB1-defect signals would not mediate sensitivity. (Reactome)
Reactome:R-HSA-9659787; FDA label 209092
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] Selection for RB1-defective clones or emergence of RB1 alterations under CDK4/6i pressure leads to resistance. (PubMed)
PMID:29236940; Reactome:R-HSA-9659787

Sensitive: [Mechanistically rare] Apparent “down” could reflect clonal composition shift toward RB-intact cells with response; drug does not repair RB1 but responding tumors can become enriched for sensitive biology. (PubMed)
PMID:35263519; Reactome:R-HSA-9659787
Resistance: [Mechanistically accurate] RB1-defect signatures may appear low in bulk yet resistance persists via other bypass routes (cyclin E/CDK2, PI3K/mTOR). (PubMed)

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High CDK4 expression (with relatively low CDK6) is described as correlating with extreme sensitivity to ribociclib, consistent with dependence on CDK4/6-mediated G1/S control.
Higher p21 (CDKN1A) levels correlate with ribociclib sensitivity and reinforce G1 arrest; loss of p21 is described in resistant models.
Cyclin D1 amplification/overexpression is described as common in HR+ tumors and linked to dependence on CDK4/6 activity, yielding pronounced arrest with CDK4/6 inhibition.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Low CDK6 is described as part of a high-CDK4/low-CDK6 expression pattern associated with heightened ribociclib sensitivity, while CDK6 overexpression is linked to resistance.
Lower Cyclin E1 activity (absence of CCNE1 amplification) is described as favoring response, whereas increased Cyclin E1/CDK2 activity bypasses CDK4/6 dependence.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: CDK6 amplification/overexpression is described as a resistance mechanism, enabling reduced dependence on CDK4-directed control despite CDK4/6 inhibition.
CCNE1 amplification/overactivity is described as driving Cyclin E/CDK2-mediated RB1 phosphorylation, bypassing CDK4/6 inhibition and correlating with poorer outcomes.
Upregulation of the Cyclin E/CDK2 axis is described as a bypass mechanism that can phosphorylate RB1 independently of CDK4/6.
p16 (CDKN2A) upregulation/amplification is described in the context of RB pathway disruption and resistance, particularly when RB1 function is compromised.
PI3K pathway activation (including PIK3CA mutations) is described as enriched in CDK4/6 inhibitor–resistant tumors and as providing alternative survival/proliferation signaling.
FGFR1 amplification is described as an upstream activator of PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK signaling, contributing to reduced dependence on CDK4/6 control and resistance.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss of functional RB1 is described as the most definitive resistance mechanism because CDK4/6 inhibitors require intact RB1 to enforce G1 arrest.
Downregulation/loss of p21 (CDKN1A) is described in resistant models and is linked to reduced enforcement of G1 arrest under CDK4/6 inhibition.
Reduced p53–p21 checkpoint activity (e.g., via TP53 mutation) is described as undermining G1 arrest and contributing to resistance.
Loss of ER signaling is described in some resistant metastatic lesions where ER expression falls, reducing hormone-driven cyclin D dependence and thereby diminishing CDK4/6 inhibitor sensitivity.
PTEN loss is described as part of PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation patterns enriched in CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance, supporting bypass survival/proliferation signaling.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Luminal A (HR+/HER2−, low proliferation): These tumors generally respond well to ribociclib + endocrine therapy, often achieving durable disease control; markers of high CDK4/cyclin D1 and intact Rb are described as common.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Luminal B (HR+/HER2−, higher proliferati: These tumors are more proliferative and are described as deriving greater absolute benefit from CDK4/6 inhibition; in CORALLEEN (luminal B), ribociclib+letrozole markedly suppressed proliferation compared to chemotherapy, and immune gene signatures in luminal B were specifically dampened by ribociclib.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-positive (HER2+/HR−): Ribociclib is described as not approved for HER2+ disease; early-phase combinations with anti-HER2 therapy (in HR+/HER2+) suggest some activity, but effects in HER2+/HR− tumors are described as unproven with no formal indication.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-negative (HR−/HER2−): TNBC is described as generally not benefiting from CDK4/6 inhibitors; many TNBC have RB loss or low RB activity and rely on CDK2/E2F or other pathways, and basal-like models show minimal response in preclinical data; not recommended outside trials.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA-mutated or HRD-positive: No indication is described that BRCA status predicts ribociclib efficacy; PARP inhibitors, not CDK4/6 inhibitors, are described as the targeted therapy in BRCA-driven breast cancer.
